How the numbers work

Likelihood is this move’s share of games with a next move on the exact path. Transpositions are not merged.

Win rate is the inspected player’s wins divided by games with that move. Draws are separate.

Branches count distinct move sequences after that move, through game end or the chosen horizon. Identical sequences count once; early endings are distinct paths.

Your preparation board

Find a Chess.com username, select a game count, then import. Full history scans all monthly archives and sets the exact maximum of available standard games.

Choose the player’s color. On the other side’s turn, the database shows opponent replies. Win rates always belong to the inspected player.

Right-click to mark a square. Right-drag to draw arrows, including L-shaped knight arrows. Hold Shift for red or Alt for blue. Left-click clears annotations. Use ← / → to navigate.

Stockfish runs on your device. Hover an engine move to preview its position or click to play through it.
